headline: Strong JOLTS lifted the 10-year to 4.95% and that one print flipped the tape inside out: the crowded shelf-and-shelter trade got liquidated while the washed-out AI complex bid.
summary: Yesterday's sequence ran in reverse. The same defensives that had been absorbing every dollar leaving mega-cap tech took the hit: XLP -2.1% after a +10.5% month at z=2.72 with acceleration 2.79, WMT -2.2% (still +19.8% on the month, z=2.95), COST -2.0%, HD -2.2%, TGT -2.5%, XRT -1.9%. Housing was worse — DHI -5.0%, ITB -3.6%, XHB -2.5%, with XHB/SPY -2.8% on the day. Meanwhile the liquidation names bounced hard: SOXX +2.5%, SMH +2.0%, AMD +3.7%, MU +2.6%, NVDA +2.3%, AVGO +3.1%, TSM +1.5%, ORCL +5.8% on its $20bn raise, MSFT +2.7%, META +2.4%. The power chain went with it — ETN +7.0%, GEV +6.5%, VST +3.7%, CEG +2.4%, GRID +1.9%. SPX +0.4%, NDX +0.7%, but RSP/SPY -0.6% and SPW -0.3%: the index rose while the median stock fell. AAPL -1.9% on margin guidance was the one mega-cap that didn't participate.

The cause is in the rates column, not the equity column. A firm JOLTS print put the 10-year up 4bp to 4.95% for a second straight session, the 30-year +4bp to 5.32%, the 5-year +4bp to 4.74%, and the 10-year real yield +3bp to 2.65%. That matters because the entire defensive/housing bid of the last month was a duration trade: 10y -33bp and 30y -31bp on the month (z=-1.41 and -1.47, acceleration -2.29 and -2.02 — a stretched rally, not a new trend). TLT -0.8% with acceleration z=+1.69 inside a down trend. The 30-year mortgage is still 7.24%, +21bp on the month, and homebuilders were never trading that number. Strip the duration tailwind and the shelter trade has no engine.

The genuine improvement is in credit and vol. The credit & vol composite went -54 to -35 and the risk regime -17 to -14. HYG +0.1%, HYG/IEF +0.5% and turning up off z=-1.65 (was -1.94), BKLN +0.2% at the 97th percentile of its year, LQD flat. VIX -1.5% to 20.83, VIX3M -1.5% to 21.27, SKEW -1.8% to 150.01. Risk appetite returned at the factor level too: high-beta/low-vol +2.3%, growth/value +1.4%, industrials/utilities +1.5%, ARKK +1.7%, IPO +2.4%, BTC +1.1%, COIN +5.5%, MSTR +3.7%. Korea confirmed — KOSPI +2.2%, EWY +2.3% — even with USDKRW +1.4%.

One session does not repair the structure. VIX/VIX3M is still 0.979 at z=1.72 and turning up; VIX is +36.1% on the month; MOVE is 99.97. RSP/SPY remains at z=3.34 with acceleration 3.76, QQQ/SPY at z=-2.72, MTUM -13.8% on the month at z=-2.61 — dispersion is still historic, it just stopped widening. SOXX is -21.0% on the month, SMH -17.8%, EWT -2.4% today. The deflation trade in hard assets deepened again: platinum -2.8% at the 0th percentile, silver -2.0% (-17.1% on the month), copper -2.2% to 6.40, gold -0.8% to 3938, gold/silver +1.2% to 79.21 at z=2.11 with acceleration 1.30, GDX -2.0%, REMX -21.3% on the month. And the new crack is Brazil: BVSP -1.4% to -13.8% on the month at z=-2.79, EWZ -16.9% and 14.3% below its 200-day, USDBRL +1.0% to 5.4883 (+5.1% on the month, z=1.48). Oil kept slipping on negotiation headlines — Brent -0.6% to 104.10, -8.6% on the week — while XLE still sits 14.3% above its 200-day at the 88th percentile. That gap is unfinished business.

good.text: Credit stopped dissenting. HYG/IEF +0.5% and turning up off z=-1.65, HYG +0.1%, BKLN +0.2% at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range. The credit & vol composite halved back from -54 to -35.
Semis found a bid at a 2-sigma washout: SOXX +2.5%, SMH +2.0%, AMD +3.7%, MU +2.6%, NVDA +2.3%, AVGO +3.1%, TSM +1.5% — and it was global, with KOSPI +2.2% and EWY +2.3%.
Speculative appetite reopened: high-beta/low-vol +2.3%, growth/value +1.4%, ARKK +1.7%, IPO +2.4%, BTC +1.1%, COIN +5.5%, MSTR +3.7%. All had been one-way lower for six sessions.
Volatility came off across the surface: VIX -1.5% to 20.83, VIX3M -1.5% to 21.27, SKEW -1.8% to 150.01, MOVE -0.4%.
The AI-power complex, left for dead, printed the biggest single-day moves on the board: ETN +7.0%, GEV +6.5%, VST +3.7%, CEG +2.4%, GRID +1.9% after GRID's -8.5% month at z=-1.64.
Pump prices keep deflating and breakevens stay anchored: gasoline -10.8% on the month at z=-1.09, 10y breakeven 2.30 (-6bp on the month), 5y 2.39. Growth pulse composite +18.

bad.text: Yields are backing up again on firm labour data: 10y +4bp to 4.95%, 30y +4bp to 5.32%, 5y +4bp to 4.74%, 10y real 2.65%. TLT -0.8%. The 30-year mortgage is still 7.24%, +21bp on the month.

The month's safety bid turned into supply in a single session: XLP -2.1% (+10.5% month, z=2.72), WMT -2.2%, COST -2.0%, HD -2.2%, DHI -5.0%, ITB -3.6%, XHB -2.5%. These positions are crowded and now price-sensitive to every basis point.

Hard-asset deflation re-accelerated: platinum -2.8% at the 0th percentile, silver -2.0% (-17.1% month, z=-1.91), copper -2.2%, gold -0.8%, gold/silver 79.21 at z=2.11 with acceleration 1.30, GDX -2.0%, GDXJ -2.1%, REMX -21.3% on the month.

Brazil is breaking, and it's accelerating: BVSP -1.4% to -13.8% on the month at z=-2.79, EWZ -16.9% and 14.3% below its 200-day, USDBRL +1.0% to 5.4883 (+5.1% month, z=1.48). EEM/SPY -7.9% on the month at z=-1.91.
The vol term structure never un-inverted: VIX/VIX3M 0.979 at z=1.72 and still turning up, VIX +36.1% on the month, MOVE at 99.97 and +28.9% over three months. Hedges remain expensive and fragile.

Index-level dispersion is still at records — RSP/SPY z=3.34 with acceleration 3.76, QQQ/SPY z=-2.72, MTUM -13.8% on the month at z=-2.61. One green day in semis does not repair SOXX -21.0% on the month.

trades.name: Short TLT / short duration
trades.line: Short TLT: the duration rally that fed defensives has stalled
trades.expr: Buy TLT Dec 80 puts, or short TLT at 81.11 against a 2.5% stop; alternatively pay 10y via ZN futures short.
trades.thesis: The 33bp monthly rally in the 10-year was a stretched, decelerating move (z=-1.41, acceleration -2.29), not a new trend. Firm job-openings data has reversed it two sessions running and the long end is leading higher, with the 30-year at 5.32% and the 10-year real yield at 2.65%. MOVE at 100 says the bond market is not done repricing.
trades.trigger: 10y +4bp to 4.95% and 30y +4bp to 5.32% today, second straight up-day; TLT -0.8% with acceleration z=+1.69 inside a down trend; mortgage 7.24% refuses to follow Treasuries lower.
trades.stop: 10y closes back below 4.80% or TLT trades above 83.

trades.name: Long XLY vs short XLP
trades.line: Long XLY / short XLP: fade the 2.7-sigma staples melt-up
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XLY, short XLP. Size 1.5% of NAV per leg.
trades.thesis: Staples are the most overbought defensive on the board after a +10.5% month at z=2.72 with acceleration 2.79, sitting at the 89th percentile — a bond proxy bought for the wrong reason. With yields turning back up, the duration support disappears. Discretionary is the mirror: XLY/XLP sits at just the 11.6th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.trigger: XLP -2.1% today, its first real down day, with WMT -2.2% (z=2.95), COST -2.0%, MCD z=2.62 and acceleration 3.38; XLY/XLP +1.4% off the lows.
trades.stop: XLY/XLP closes below 1.290, or XLP makes a new high.

trades.name: Long SMH call spread
trades.line: Long SMH Dec call spread on the 2-sigma semi washout
trades.expr: Buy SMH Dec 530/580 call spread for defined risk; add cash SMH only on a hold above today's low.
trades.thesis: SOXX -21.0% and SMH -17.8% on the month at z=-2.37/-2.17 is a liquidation, not a fundamental re-rate, and today it stopped. Credit confirmed the turn (HYG/IEF +0.5% off z=-1.65) and Asia confirmed it (KOSPI +2.2%, EWY +2.3%). Defined risk because the trend state is still 'rolling over' and SMH/SPY remains 3.6% below its 200-day.
trades.trigger: SOXX +2.5%, SMH +2.0%, AMD +3.7%, MU +2.6%, NVDA +2.3%, AVGO +3.1% on the day; SMH/SPY +1.7% off a -16.1% monthly drawdown.
trades.stop: SMH closes below 490, or SMH/SPY makes a new closing low beneath 0.675.
trades.target: SMH 570 (back above the 200-day near 520 and into the gap).

trades.name: Long EWW vs short EWZ
trades.line: Long EWW / short EWZ: Mexico compounds, Brazil cracks
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long EWW, short EWZ. 1.5% per leg.
trades.thesis: LatAm has split cleanly. Mexico: MXX +8.8% on the month at z=1.92 and 4.0% above its 200-day, EWW +5.1%. Brazil: BVSP -13.8% at z=-2.79 with acceleration -2.32, EWZ -16.9% and 14.3% below its 200-day, with the currency confirming — USDBRL +5.1% on the month at z=1.48 and turning up. Local-currency stress plus index breakdown is the classic EM unwind pattern.
trades.trigger: Today: BVSP -1.4%, EWZ -1.3%, USDBRL +1.0% to 5.4883 (52-week 85th percentile), versus MXX +0.6%.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.25, or EWZ reclaims its 50-day and the spread goes -5%.

trades.name: Short XLE into stale marks
trades.line: Short XLE: 14% above 200d while Brent is -8.6% on the week
trades.expr: Short XLE at 66.68, or buy XLE Dec 65/60 put spread. Keep it small against a long XOM if you need sector carry.
trades.thesis: Energy equity has caught down only part of the barrel's move. XLE is still +6.1% on the month and 14.3% above its 200-day at the 88th percentile; XOM 15.3% and CVX 17.4% above their 200-days at the 89th percentile. Brent is -8.6% on the week with negotiation headlines pressing, and gasoline is -10.8% on the month at z=-1.09, which is the demand-side tell.
trades.trigger: XLE -0.8%, XOP -1.1%, XOM -1.2%, CVX -1.1% today on a day the S&P rose 0.4% — relative supply, not beta; OIH rolling over after -5.8% on the week.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 110 or XLE closes above 70.

trades.name: Short LMT vs long ITA
trades.line: Short LMT / long ITA: fade the board's most extreme z-score
trades.expr: Short LMT, long ITA, dollar-neutral. 1% per leg.
trades.thesis: LMT +26.4% on the month at z=3.41 with acceleration 3.05 is the single most stretched reading in the digest, 13.3% above its 200-day at the 88th percentile, with relative strength +29.0% in a month. The sector it belongs to has done nothing: ITA +4.0% on the month, 5.3% below its 200-day, -13.7% over three months. This is single-name crowding, and it mean-reverts without needing a view on defense spending.
trades.trigger: LMT -0.6% today while ITA +0.7% — the first day the spread went the other way since the melt-up started.
trades.stop: LMT makes a new closing high, or the pair goes -4%.

trades.name: Long GRID / electrification basket
trades.line: Long GRID: power chain bottoming as semis stop bleeding
trades.expr: Long GRID at 167.40, or an equal-weight basket of ETN, GEV, VST, CEG.
trades.thesis: The AI-power complex was liquidated with the semis — GRID -8.5% on the month at z=-1.64 and 6.0% below its 200-day, NLR -12.4% at the 0.5 percentile, VST at the 9th percentile. If the semi liquidation is ending, the second-derivative trade is the electrical chain, which carries real order books, not multiple.
trades.trigger: Today's largest single-name moves on the board came from this group: ETN +7.0%, GEV +6.5%, VST +3.7%, CEG +2.4%, GRID +1.9% — on the same session SOXX rallied 2.5%.
trades.stop: GRID closes below 157, or VST makes a new 52-week low.
